text:
Sanjay: quick thought — current spillover is too binary: when pool full we immediately migrate to fallback which causes oscillation and hotspots. what if we used time-decayed spillover tokens per tenant + short, rate-limited migration windows to smooth it out?

Claire: can you sketch how tokens are earned/consumed? worried about starving bursty tenants.

Sanjay: tokens accumulate when tenant is under its soft-reservation, decaying with half-life. consuming happens on migration events; if tokens insufficient we queue and try again in next window. goal: avoid immediate full-pool drain when many tenants spike.

Matt: sounds promising. two quick asks: 1) asymmetric behavior for scale-up vs scale-down — prefer conservative backoff on scale-down. 2) make token decay configurable per-tier (enterprise vs free).

Sanjay: agree on asymmetry. also propose rate-limited migration window: default 5s windows, max migrations per-window = floor(min_tokens * alpha). keeps admission smooth.

Claire: how does this interact with SLA routing? e.g., p99-sensitive routes shouldn't be queued.

Sanjay: annotate routes with "latency_class": {"gold","standard"}. gold bypasses queue (but consumes emergency token bucket, smaller capacity). standard follows token flow.

Matt: pseudo-config idea:
```yaml
migration_policy:
  window: 5s
  token_half_life: 30m
  per_tier:
    enterprise:
      token_rate: 2/s
      emergency_bucket: 10
    free:
      token_rate: 0.2/s
      emergency_bucket: 1
  asymmetry:
    scale_up_multiplier: 2.0
    scale_down_multiplier: 0.5
```

Claire: nice. metrics we should track: per-tenant tokens, migrations_per_window, queued_migrations, p95/p99 delta post-migration, and cost impact. also add a circuit breaker if queued_migrations > threshold.

Matt: +1 to circuit breaker. also we need an operator-visible fallback: a forced-drain command that bypasses token flow for emergency ops (with audit log).

infra-bot: deploy-canary started for cluster us-west-2 with feature-flag "spillover_tokens_v1" on 1759510200.

ops-bot: alert rule suggestion: "spillover_queue_surge" fires if queued_migrations > 50 for > 2m. severity: P2.

Claire: test plan: 1) unit tests for decay math; 2) small-scale chaos: 50 tenants ramp to 10x, verify no more than 3x spike in migrations; 3) prod canary in one shard for 24h, monitor p99 and cost.

Sanjay: i'll draft RFC with math, config knobs, and a PoC impl in the operator. tagging @Matt and @Claire for review. plan to start PoCing next week. :+1:

Matt: thanks — assign to the "pool-orch-refactor" board and drop RFC link here once ready.

Sanjay: will do.

infra-bot: canary completed on 1759510400 — no immediate errors, telemetry forwarded to #eng-runtime-observability.

ops-bot: note — add audit log entry when emergency_bucket used (who triggered & reason).

Claire: one more note: we should simulate cost-model: tokens allowing spillover might increase transient egress to cheaper pools but could raise total GPU-hours. include cost sweep in RFC.

Sanjay: good call, will include cost sweep and threshold knobs. closing thread to convert into RFC doc.
